title: Invented example headlines
subject: PSHE
unit: Spring 2: Who likes chocolate? Global trade, media and stereotyping
source: Written for pshe/y6 lesson 15 (Invented example headlines (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 15: Reporting the news: media and stereotyping, and review. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

blocks.h: Invented headlines: same event, two ways

head: Event
Headline A
Headline B
rows: Wonderful new park brings families together
Council wastes money on another park
Brave team so close to victory
A school changes its lunch menu
Pupils furious as favourite foods are banned

questions.q: For each event, which words show bias?
questions.a: Park: 'wonderful', 'wastes', 'another'. Football: 'brave', 'so close', 'hopeless', 'crashes out again'. Lunch: 'wins praise', 'furious', 'banned'.
For example: 'New park opens in the town centre'; 'Team loses 2-1'; 'School changes its lunch menu'.

keywords.def: the title of a news story
an unfair idea that a whole group is the same
someone who questions what they read

questions.q: Rewrite fairly: 'Noisy teenagers cause trouble at library.'
questions.a: 'Teenagers meet at library for study group.' (if that is the fact)

questions.q: Review (pupil PDF): six questions on the unit, then rewrite one biased headline fairly.
questions.a: Six answers and a fair headline.

questions.q: Extend: explain how one word can change a whole story.
questions.a: Words like 'lazy' or 'heroic' make readers judge before the facts.
A) 'Lazy workers ruin harvest'. 'Lazy' is a loaded word that stereotypes.

questions.q: Think again: Two headlines report the same event differently. How can that change what people think?
questions.a: Word choice can make a group look good or bad; a critical reader notices.
